The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of three line segments. Then,

${\int }_{-6}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of three parts: the line segment for $x\in [-6,-2],$ the line segment for $x\in (-2,1],$ and the line segment for $x\in (1,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-6}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-6,-2].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+5)4 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-2,1].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,4].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+1)3 \\  & =7.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =12+6+7.5 \\  & =25.5.\end{aligned}
$$
